category: AI導入の判断、ガバナンス、事業成果
title: Prioritizing Use Cases
prompt: The customer support and billing teams have proposed two generative AI pilots. One could have a large impact, but its data agreements have not been sorted out; the other could have a smaller impact, but is ready to proceed. How should these options be evaluated so the executive committee can make a decision?

choices.text: Choose based only on the projected first-year savings.
choices.explanation: This does not account for whether the data can be used, implementation costs, or the scale of the impact.

choices.text: Compare business value, data readiness, implementation difficulty, and risk.
choices.explanation: This considers both the expected benefits and the feasibility of realizing them.

choices.text: Always choose the use case that can use the largest model.
choices.explanation: Model size does not indicate business value or implementation feasibility.

choices.text: Choose the use case with the most stakeholders.
choices.explanation: The number of users alone does not reveal a use case’s outcomes or risks.

learning.reason: This considers both the expected benefits and the feasibility of realizing them.
learning.concept: Start with a problem that can be tested on a small scale and has measurable criteria for deciding whether to continue or stop.

category: AI導入の判断、ガバナンス、事業成果
title: Measuring Business Outcomes
prompt: A contact center wants AI assistance to shorten call times, without increasing repeat contacts caused by incorrect guidance. What should it prepare before starting the pilot?

choices.text: Record only the number of model parameters.
choices.explanation: Model size is not a baseline for business outcomes.

choices.text: Set a target only for the activation rate of the new tool.
choices.explanation: Adoption can be measured, but there is no basis for comparing business impact and quality.

choices.text: Establish baselines and targets for measures such as current handling time and resolution quality.
choices.explanation: This makes it possible to compare performance before and after implementation using consistent measures.

choices.text: Collect only favorable comments after launch.
choices.explanation: This introduces selection bias and provides no comparison with the pre-launch state.

learning.reason: This makes it possible to compare performance before and after implementation using consistent measures.
learning.concept: Combine efficiency measures with quality measures, such as incorrect guidance and repeat contacts.

title: Human Review Before Final Decisions
prompt: Generative AI will draft notices that affect customers’ rights. If a notice cites an incorrect policy, correcting it after it is sent is difficult. Which control is appropriate before sending?

choices.text: Have a staff member check the supporting evidence and the wording, then approve the notice before it is sent.
choices.explanation: This retains human judgment for outputs that could have serious consequences.

choices.text: Automatically send any notice whose wording appears to have high model confidence.
choices.explanation: Fluent wording does not guarantee correctness.

choices.text: Rely only on audit logs to manage the risks of automatic sending.
choices.explanation: Logs can support an after-the-fact review, but they do not prevent an incorrect notice from being sent.

choices.text: Automatically send the notices, then have a person audit a sample the next day.
choices.explanation: This allows evaluation, but does not stop an irreversible notice before it is sent.

learning.reason: This retains human judgment for outputs that could have serious consequences.
learning.concept: Define who reviews each output, the approval criteria, and the process for sending it back for revision according to its impact.

title: Preparing Data for Use
prompt: An internal search pilot includes documents that cannot be used for purposes outside their contractual terms, personal information, and public materials. Public materials and approved internal materials are sufficient for development. What should be done first?

choices.text: Shorten the prompts to manage confidentiality.
choices.explanation: Input length does not establish whether data may be used or how it must be handled.

choices.text: Input all documents at once and check the restrictions afterward.
choices.explanation: This could result in using content without permission.

choices.text: Index all materials and display a warning in the search results.
choices.explanation: Indexing or sending the data could already exceed the contractual restrictions on its use.

choices.text: Classify the data and limit it to what is needed for the purpose and permitted for use.
choices.explanation: This makes it possible to check the data’s confidentiality and usage terms against the intended purpose.

learning.reason: This makes it possible to check the data’s confidentiality and usage terms against the intended purpose.
learning.concept: Decide from the outset how to verify the purpose of use, access scope, retention period, and whether data will be sent to third parties.

title: Implementation Costs and Benefits
prompt: Pilot measurements for summarization showed that drafting time per item decreased, but operation now requires human corrections and quality audits. The business unit is deciding on next quarter’s investment. What should it compare?

choices.text: Compare the value of the time saved with the total costs of inference, operations, and review.
choices.explanation: This evaluates business benefits and ongoing costs using the same basis.

choices.text: Compare only the initial development effort during the pilot.
choices.explanation: This does not capture the costs and benefits of continued use.

choices.text: Count only the reduction in generation time as a benefit, excluding the time people spend making corrections.
choices.explanation: This overstates the benefits realized across the entire process.

choices.text: Decide solely based on the model with the lowest price per token.
choices.explanation: This leaves rework, quality differences, and operating costs out of the evaluation.

learning.reason: This evaluates business benefits and ongoing costs using the same basis.
learning.concept: State assumptions about volume, retries, and review rates, and estimate how costs change as usage grows.

category: AI導入の判断、ガバナンス、事業成果
title: Decision After a Pilot
prompt: A pilot in a limited number of service channels met its processing-time target but exceeded the threshold for serious incorrect guidance. The business owner must decide whether the solution can be expanded safely. What should they do next?

choices.text: Roll it out everywhere as long as overall average satisfaction remains steady.
choices.explanation: This replaces the threshold for serious errors with an average metric.

choices.text: Analyze the causes of serious errors, limit the scope, and reassess until they are within the acceptable range.
choices.explanation: This reflects both efficiency and quality in the expansion decision.

choices.text: Expand to all operations based solely on meeting the time target.
choices.explanation: This widens the scope while serious failures remain.

choices.text: Make usage volume the only new success metric.
choices.explanation: This does not reveal or control the quality problem.

learning.reason: This reflects both efficiency and quality in the expansion decision.
learning.concept: Set success criteria and stop conditions before expansion, and do not let an overall average obscure failures in important cases.

category: AI導入の判断、ガバナンス、事業成果
title: Causality and Sustained Business Outcomes
prompt: A department that rolled out agent assistance reduced processing time by 15%. During the same period, a pricing change increased the number of simple inquiries, and quality audit results are not yet available. Which evaluation is needed for the next investment decision?

choices.text: Use a comparison group with similar inquiry types and workload, and measure both repeat-inquiry rates and processing time.
choices.explanation: This separates apparent improvement caused by a change in the mix of inquiries and can also detect a decline in quality.

choices.text: Apply the reduction rate across the company and commit to the investment.
choices.explanation: This does not separate the rollout’s effect from the change in inquiry mix.

choices.text: Compare before and after results using only the best-performing employees.
choices.explanation: Selection bias and changes in the inquiry mix remain.

choices.text: Use the number of times the assistance tool is used as a KPI and treat it as an outcome.
choices.explanation: This shows adoption but is not directly tied to business outcomes.

learning.reason: This separates apparent improvement caused by a change in the mix of inquiries and can also detect a decline in quality.
learning.concept: Define business KPIs in advance for a pilot, and include a control group and quality guardrails.

title: Sequencing Rollouts by Risk Level
prompt: The same foundation model is being considered for summarizing internal meeting minutes and advising on whether customers should be approved for loans. Executives want to see benefits soon, but they do not allow automation of high-impact decisions before validation.

choices.text: Because the model is the same, use the same approval process for both business activities and roll them out at the same time.
choices.explanation: This does not account for the difference in impact between use contexts.

choices.text: Automate the loan use case first because its benefits are greater, and measure quality afterward.
choices.explanation: This automates a high-risk use case before validation, which is not allowed.

choices.text: Assess the suitability of the loan use case based only on the cost of summarizing meeting minutes.
choices.explanation: This substitutes one decision for assessments of different outcomes and risks.

choices.text: Classify use cases by impact, roll out lower-risk activities first, and design validation and human approval for high-risk use cases in advance.
choices.explanation: This balances phased value realization with controls proportionate to risk.

learning.reason: This balances phased value realization with controls proportionate to risk.
learning.concept: In addition to model-level approval, define the intended use, impact, and stop conditions for each business activity.

title: Identify the cause of low adoption
prompt: The support AI meets the quality standards, but frontline adoption is low. Users report more copying into a separate tab and say the exception-handling process is unclear. What should be prioritized?

choices.text: Increase only the model size
choices.explanation: The problem lies in the workflow, not in model quality.

choices.text: Redesign the workflow with frontline staff, integrate the AI into existing tools, and clarify exception ownership and training
choices.explanation: This reduces workflow friction and operational uncertainty, making it possible to evaluate the benefits of adoption.

choices.text: Pause quality audits until adoption improves
choices.explanation: Reducing safety does not remove workflow barriers.

choices.text: Require everyone to use the AI while leaving the workflow unchanged
choices.explanation: Usage may increase, but the extra work and exception-handling issues will remain.

learning.reason: This reduces workflow friction and operational uncertainty, making it possible to evaluate the benefits of adoption.
learning.concept: Assess adoption problems by separating model quality, workflow integration, and ownership and training.

title: Align data terms for AI vendors
prompt: The sales department is comparing several AI vendors. Because customer inputs will be used, it wants to manage deletion deadlines and secondary use for retraining by contract, and obtain audit evidence in case it needs to switch vendors.

choices.text: Require vendors to encrypt data and nothing more
choices.explanation: Encryption does not define secondary use or deletion deadlines.

choices.text: Choose the lowest-priced candidate and review the contract after the pilot
choices.explanation: Data already submitted could be retained under terms that have not been reviewed.

choices.text: Make retention, deletion, secondary use, and audit access acceptance criteria, and compare each candidate’s contract and operational evidence
choices.explanation: This evaluates the organization’s data controls independently of price and performance.

choices.text: Measure only accuracy with input-output tests
choices.explanation: This cannot assess contractual terms for retention or secondary use.

learning.reason: This evaluates the organization’s data controls independently of price and performance.
learning.concept: Vendor evaluation covers not only business outcomes but also data handling and exit requirements.
